The US power grid uses alternating current at 60Hz, so LCD monitors for that market (and others that use 60Hz AC) initially ran 60Hz. Differences between FPS and screen refresh cause tearing in the image, where the top of the screen will show one frame, and the bottom will show another. Vsync delays the display of a frame until the screen refreshes, but causes input lag for to the delay.

60 FPS is better than 30 FPS for the trains others have stated: better physics and input response. Even better than 60 FPS is variable refresh, where the display is able to redraw the image simultaneous with the system's ability to present it.
